title: Fix Hidden Middle Header Border Between Window Chips
description: In print report windows (e.g. figure/table windows like "Generator-Pipeline" / Abbildung chip), the horizontal border line that closes the transparent gap between the two header chips (title chip and hierarchy/number chip) is not visible. Root cause: the header row (title chip + gap + hierarchy chip) is typeset inline BEFORE the tcolorbox window opens, and \semio_window_vskip_stroke_hairline pulls the box up by one hairline to overlap that closing stroke — but since the tcolorbox's own colback fill is painted later in the PDF stream, it paints over (hides) that hairline-thin border stroke in the gap area between the two chips. This only affects the "unbroken" (single page-part, the common case) and the first part of genuinely broken windows, since continuation-page headers already redraw via a tcolorbox `overlay` (drawn after/on top of the box fill, via \semio@window@header@repeat) and are unaffected. Fix: redraw the header row via the same overlay mechanism for the unbroken/first case too (analogous to \semio@window@header@repeat), so it paints on top of the box fill and the border is never covered.
summary: Fixed the window header's closing baseline stroke (the horizontal border in the transparent gap between a window's title chip and hierarchy/number chip) being invisibly overpainted by the tcolorbox's own background fill. The header row is typeset inline before the box opens and pulled up by one hairline to overlap that stroke, but the box's colback fill paints later in the PDF stream and covered it. Added \semio@window@header@invoke@overlay, which redraws the header row via the same frame.north-anchored tcolorbox overlay technique already used for continuation-page headers (\semio@window@header@repeat), and wired it into the tcbset overlay~unbroken/overlay~first keys so it repaints on top of the fill for the common single-page and first-of-broken-window cases. Verified by building print/dist/report.pdf and visually inspecting the "Hierarchy Demo" / "Abbildung: 2.b" window header — the border now spans continuously across the gap.
